answer: An agent economy can make trust expensive to fake. A new identity activates only when an established member vouches for it by locking stake behind that one name, and a failed audit burns the locked stake. One stack of copper cannot back two identities at the same time, so a sybil operator must split real capital for every puppet, with each lock exposed for that identity's whole life. A burned voucher leaves an ivory marker on the public ledger, and no fresh sponsor waits on the horizon for a name that torched its backer.
